chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council Finance Committee vote, asks everyone to silence electronic devices, and yields to the chair. The opening lines refer to the Committee on Finance despite the Education Committee agenda context.
chapters.title: Finance Committee staff opens vote and yields to Chair Linda Lee

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for the Committee on Finance.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time, we please ask that you silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Moving forward, no one is approached to front desk.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Great.

chapters.summary: Linda Lee identifies herself as chair of the Committee on Finance and recognizes fellow committee members present. She lists Majority Leader Abreu, Council Members Morano, Marte, Narcisse, Sanchez, Hudson, Aldebal, Brooks-Powers, Wong, Gennaro, and others.
chapters.title: Chair Linda Lee opens Finance Committee meeting and recognizes members

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Linda Lee, Chair of the Committee on Finance.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I would like to recognize my fellow committee members.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Majority Leader Abreu, Council Members Morano and Marte and Narcisse and Jay Sanchez, Hudson, Aldebal, Brooks Powers, Wong, and I, oh, and Gennaro.

chapters.summary: Lee says the committee will consider Proposed Introduction 978-B, sponsored by Council Member Farah Louis, to raise income thresholds for senior and disabled rent-increase exemptions. She also introduces a transparency resolution to approve expense-budget designations for certain organizations.
chapters.title: Lee outlines rent-exemption bill and transparency resolution on agenda

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: At today's hearing, the committee will consider and vote on the following items.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Proposed introduction number 978B, prime sponsored by Councilmember Farrah Lewis, a local law to amend the administrative code of the City of New York

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: in relation to increasing the maximum income level qualifying for exemption from rent increases granted to certain senior citizens and persons with disabilities, and adjusting the income requirements related thereto.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: A transparency resolution.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: sponsored by myself to approve the designation and changes in the designation of certain organizations to receive funding in the expense budget,

chapters.summary: Lee announces five pre-considered resolutions approving Department of Housing Preservation and Development requests for real-property tax exemptions under Article 11. She names 300 West 17th Street, Mahaney Cluster, and Albans, identifying the affected council districts.
chapters.title: Lee lists five HPD Article 11 tax-exemption projects

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: and five pre-considered resolutions sponsored also by myself that would approve requests from the Department of Housing Preservation and Development for real property tax exemptions under Article 11 of the Private Housing Law for the following projects.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: 300 West 17th Street in the District of Councilmember Wilson, Mahaney Cluster in the Districts of Councilmembers Encarnacion, Feliz, and J.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sanchez, and Albans in the District of Deputy Speaker Williams.

chapters.summary: Lee introduces Proposed Resolution 666 to schedule a November 19, 2026 public hearing on increasing the budgets of eight existing BIDs. She lists 34th Street, 82nd Street, East Mid-Manhattan, Myrtle Avenue, Bay Ridge 5th Avenue, Southern Boulevard, Greater JFK, and West Village.
chapters.title: Lee schedules BID budget hearing and names eight BIDs

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And finally, proposed Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: 666, sponsored by myself as well, which would schedule a public hearing on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 11 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: In the Committee Room City Hall to consider legislation that would authorize an increase in the budget of eight existing bids.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: The eight bids that are seeking budget increases are 34th Street in Manhattan, 82nd Street in Queens,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: East Mid-Manhattan, Myrtle Avenue in Brooklyn, Bay Ridge 5th Avenue in Brooklyn, Southern Boulevard in the Bronx, Greater JFK in Queens, and West Village in Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Do any of my colleagues want to share any remarks on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, Councilmember Jay Sanchez.

chapters.summary: Council Member Justin Sanchez says tax exemption T2026-2688 covers repairs at 917 Eagle Avenue, a five-story walk-up with 123 recorded violations including 41 Class C violations. Across 14 Manny properties in his district, he cites 524 additional violations, including 164 Class C, 92 vermin-related, 16 lead, 15 roof, 17 heat or hot-water, mold, exposed wiring, and self-closing door issues.
chapters.title: Sanchez details 917 Eagle Avenue and Manny portfolio violations

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lee.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: So today's vote on T2026-2688 is providing a tax exemption specifically for repairs to 917

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Eagle Avenue, a walk-up building that is only five stories tall but has 123 recorded violations, including 41 Class C violations.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: According to across the 14 Manny properties in my district, Manny is responsible for fixing an additional 524 recorded housing violations.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Of those, 164 additional violations are Class C violations, the most serious classification of housing violations in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: 92 class C violations involving rats, rodents, and other vermin.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: 16 instances where lead was found.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: 15 roof-related issues.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: 17 units without heat or hot water.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: 5 with mold and 4 with exposed electrical wires.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: And 17 self-closing door issues which put the safety of the entire building at risk if any of those wires created a fire.

chapters.summary: Sanchez argues the violations are not spreadsheet entries but daily living conditions for families. He says tax exemptions cannot be handed out without accountability and that developers and property managers must maintain safe, stable homes after tenants move in.
chapters.title: Sanchez says violations show tenants lack safe, dignified homes

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Think about what those numbers mean for the families living there.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: These aren't just violations on a spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: These are the conditions people are expected to come home to every single day.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: We cannot simply hand out tax exemptions without accountability and expect that all the problems will just disappear.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: When we talk about building more affordable housing, I want to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: That the job of the developer, the property manager, the council member, and everybody else involved does not end once it's built and the tenant moves in.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: The key to the door should unlock a safe, stable, and dignified home where you can build your future and rest your head at every night, knowing the roof is not about to cave in over you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says the cluster extends beyond his district and a no vote would put colleagues in a difficult position, so he abstains on T2026-2688 and accompanying resolutions. He says Manny provided a repair plan and timeline, but residents deserve independently verified repairs, and he warns future abatement applicants in the 17th District to bring maintenance plans.
chapters.title: Sanchez abstains on Mahaney cluster and warns future tax-break applicants

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This cluster goes beyond the boundaries of my district, and I understand that a vote against it would put my colleagues in a difficult position.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, I will abstain from this vote because I want to make clear that this is not the standard in the 17th.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: We will not give out tax breaks.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: And handouts to people and organizations who are not doing the work that they pledged to do.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: I demanded that Manny provide a clear plan and timeline to address these conditions.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Manny did so in advance of my decision on how to vote today.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Manny told our office that these violations will be corrected, but residents deserve more than promises and paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: They deserve independently verified repairs and lasting solutions.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Manny has a responsibility to maintain their properties, and with this exemption that is likely to pass, they need to ensure that every dollar that they are not paying the city is going towards repairs and directly improving the quality of life of their tenants.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: This is a direct signal to future applicants of tax abatements in my district.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: If you need city subsidies to maintain your buildings, I expect you to come to us with a plan on how you are planning to maintain all of your properties in the 17th.

chapters.summary: After a brief interruption about voting, Lee notes that Council Members Ressler, Felice, and Felder have joined the meeting and asks whether anyone else has remarks. With no further comments, she calls the vote.
chapters.title: Lee acknowledges late-arriving members and calls the vote

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: In Council District.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I vote aye on everything I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No, we're not voting yet.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, and we've also been joined by Council Members Ressler as well as Felice.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And does anyone else have any comments or remarks?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Oh, and Council Member Felder.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I think with that, we can call the vote.

chapters.summary: Finance Committee Clerk Ben Jacobs starts the roll call. Chair Lee votes aye, and Council Member Brooks-Powers asks to explain her vote, disclosing a family member associated with the Department of Education before voting aye.
chapters.title: Clerk begins roll call; Brooks-Powers discloses DOE family tie

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Committee on Finance, Ben Jacobs, Committee Clerk, the roll call vote for all a couple of items.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Lee.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Aye and all.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member General.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Brooks-Fowers.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Brooks Powers.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Permission granted.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I'd like to disclose on the record that we are moving funds with the Department of Education, and I have a family member associated with that entity, and with that I vote aye or no.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: The clerk continues through committee members, with several aye votes. Sanchez votes aye on all items except 2688 and accompanying resolutions, on which he abstains; Wong votes aye on all; Morano votes aye except no on the transparency resolution.
chapters.title: Roll call continues; Sanchez abstains on 2688 and Morano opposes transparency

utterances.text: Council Member Felice.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Rao?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Velas.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Hudson.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Mealy.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Narcisse.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Averay.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Williams.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Eldable.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Maloney.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: I vote aye on all with the exception of 2688 for which I abstain.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: And any accompanying resolutions.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Council Member Wong.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I vote aye on all.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Morano.

chapters.summary: The clerk announces that all items except the Mahaney cluster land-use item and the transparency resolution passed 13-0. The transparency resolution passed 12-1 with no abstentions, and the Mahaney cluster passed 12-0 with one abstention; all items are adopted.
chapters.title: Clerk reports adoption of items with one abstention and one no vote

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So that is on all items except for the

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: land use item, the Mahaney cluster, and the transparency for all items is 13-0 except for the transparency resolution, which is 12 in the affirmative, 1 in the negative, no abstentions,

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: and the Mahaney cluster land use item, which is 12 in the affirmative, none in the negative, and 1 abstention.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: The items are adopted.

chapters.summary: Lee thanks participants and concludes the Finance Committee vote. The meeting ends after the roll-call results are announced.
chapters.title: Chair Lee concludes Finance Committee vote

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much, and that concludes the Finance Committee vote.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Finance Committee held a vote on Int. 978-B, a transparency resolution, five HPD Article 11 tax-exemption resolutions, and Res. 666 scheduling a BID budget hearing.

Council Member Justin Sanchez detailed severe housing violations at 917 Eagle Avenue and across Manny properties, abstaining on the Mahaney cluster tax exemption while warning future abatement applicants.
The committee adopted all items: most passed 13-0, the transparency resolution passed 12-1, and the Mahaney cluster passed 12-0 with one abstention.
